title: Audit ingest: observed-QoS-driven tiering and retention safeguards
creator: Amelia Chen
description: Implement an adaptive ingestion and storage policy for audit logs that enforces cost controls while preserving high-value security signals (RBAC v2 admin events, SSO/SAML flows, and privileged operations). Goals: 1) move from static time-only retention to an observed-QoS-driven hot/cold tiering model; 2) reduce hot-path storage costs via compact indexing and probabilistic filters without degrading common investigative workflows; 3) surface safety nets (soft quotas, circuit breakers) to prevent runaway ingest costs during spikes (e.g., SSO flood or role migration bug). Scope: ingest pipeline changes (partitioning keys, sequence-level metadata), storage format decisions (segment size, compression, index shape), retention automation (per-event-type TTLs and TTL overrides for legal holds), and operator controls in Console for quota/eviction policy tuning. Must capture RBAC v2 and SSO events with enriched context (actor id, role delta, session id, request trace) and preserve cryptographic integrity (signed segments + KMS-managed encryption keys).
comments: 2025-07-11 — Kickoff: Security, Observability, and Storage teams aligned on goals. Agreed to prototype with a two-tier model (hot=7d, warm=30d) and evaluate dynamic promotion based on query heat and SLA metrics.

2025-07-17 — Design review notes (PM + Sec): Add explicit retention categories: admin-critical (RBAC v2 changes, SSO failure spikes), auth-transactions (sign-ins), and telemetry (low-signal events). PM asked for per-customer SLA overrides and legal hold path.

2025-07-25 — Engineering spike complete: validated time+size-based partitioning with 512MB segment targets reduces shard count by ~18% in our test traces. Prototype uses Parquet+ZSTD for cold segments and compact Avro for hot writes to allow fast append and small-read latency.

2025-08-02 — Trade-off discussion: Full-text indexing of payloads gives powerful forensic queries but increases storage 2.5x. Decided to keep structured indices (actor, event_type, role_id, trace_id) + bloom filters for payload presence checks, and offer optional full-text indexing as a paid feature per-customer.

2025-08-09 — Observability: Created Grafana dashboard 'audit.ingest.qos' to show ingest rate, hot-segment fill, average query latency for investigations, and cost burn rate. Early signal: a customer SSO migration test caused 4x normal ingest; circuit breaker prototype throttled non-admin events and prioritized RBAC v2 changes.

2025-08-14 — Security review prep: Documented KMS key rotation plan and segment signing spec for tamper-evidence. Security requested a minimal schema versioning header per-segment to support forward/backwards compatibility.

2025-08-20 — PRs: internal infra PR (https://github.com/redwood-inference/infer-platform/pull/1284) adds time+size partitioner and segment metadata write path. Storage PR (https://github.com/redwood-inference/storage/pull/557) adds cold-store eviction job and cost accounting hooks.

2025-08-25 — QA runs: ingestion spike tests and query smoke validated retention overrides and legal-hold retrieval. Found edge-case: role-change events were lumped with high-volume telemetry under the current event_type mapping; created subtasks to enrich event taxonomy (ENG-91502).
2025-08-28 — Next steps: finalize operator Console controls (soft-quota UI + emergency-evict button), complete security review, and schedule rollout to stage cluster for two-week validation window.

Review feedback (2025-07-17 — from Priya Desai, Product): Provide migration guidance for Dedicated customers with existing index layout. Also add cost visibility in Console (projected 90-day spend with current policy vs proposed).
Action item (2025-08-26 — from Observability): Add trace sampling tag to retained hot events so cross-product traces are joinable without keeping full request bodies by default.
